_readme: Physical parameters used by the physics core. Every entry: value, unit, and either 'source' (published figure) or 'estimate' (reasoned assumption, with the reasoning). Edit freely; the lab and tests read this file.

gamma_air.source: ratio of specific heats, dry air

T_air.source: about -1 C, air temperature reported 14 Apr 1912 (British Inquiry)

Cd_sharp_orifice.source: sharp-edged orifice discharge coefficient (standard hydraulics texts)

Cd_doorway.estimate: rounded doorway with frame; between sharp orifice (0.61) and short tube (0.8)

Leff_factor.estimate: inertial length of the jet region ~0.85 sqrt(A) per side (orifice added-length approximation)

door_leak_fraction.estimate: gaps round a closed non-watertight cabin door (~3 mm all round a 0.8 x 2 m door)

cabin_door_mass.estimate: panelled hardwood door 0.76 x 1.98 x 0.045 m at ~480 kg/m^3 plus fittings

cabin_latch_strength.estimate: mortice latch bolt and keeper in wood: typical failure 1.5-3 kN

cabin_hinge_strength.estimate: brass butt hinge screwed into hardwood frame

frame_stop_strength.estimate: door stop/rebate bearing the whole leaf when pushed closed

manila_3in_breaking_load.source: 3-inch circumference manila, ~4 short tons minimum breaking strength (US Navy rope tables)

manila_EA.estimate: axial stiffness: ~10-12 % elongation at breaking load for new manila

fall_parts.unit: parts of rope supporting the load
fall_parts.estimate: Titanic boat falls rove through double/single blocks; 3 supporting parts assumed

length.source: 30 ft wooden lifeboats (Harland & Wolff), British Inquiry

hull_mass.estimate: clinker-built yellow pine boat with gear and air tanks; published figures 1.2-1.5 t

person_mass.estimate: 1912 adult average incl. heavy winter clothing

leather_on_dry_teak.estimate: leather sole on oiled teak/pine deck

plate_glass_strength.source: annealed plate glass design flexural strength ~41 MPa (short duration)

window_glass_thickness.estimate: 3/8 inch plate glass in B-deck windows

Ca_hull_heave.estimate: flat-bottomed boat heaving at the surface
